title: Speculative Generation

book.title: NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails Library Developer Guide

description: Run input rails and main LLM generation concurrently to reduce end-to-end latency.
content:
Speculative Generation Speculative generation executes input-rail evaluation concurrently with main LLM response generation instead of serializing the two operations
When response generation takes longer than input-rail evaluation, speculative generation hides the input-rail latency from the end-to-end response time
While it can reduce the end-to-end latency, this optimization starts the main LLM call for requests that input rails later classify as unsafe, which can increase token usage
Output rails still validate every response before delivery, so users do not receive responses that output rails block. Early-release Feature Speculative generation is an early-release IORails engine feature
The IORails engine supports speculative generation only for non-streaming requests ( generate_async
Streaming requests ( stream_async ) use sequential execution and emit a warning. When to Use Speculative Generation Use speculative generation when most requests are expected to pass input rails and input-rail latency contributes meaningfully to end-to-end response time
In this case, the IORails engine can overlap input-rail evaluation with the main LLM call, reducing latency for safe requests from approximately input rail latency + generation latency to approximately max(input rail latency, generation latency) . This feature is most useful when unsafe requests are rare and the additional token cost for rejected requests is acceptable
For example, if 2% of requests are unsafe, the engine might generate and discard tokens for those requests, while the remaining 98% benefit from concurrent input-rail evaluation and response generation. Avoid speculative generation when unsafe traffic is frequent, token cost is more important than latency, or your workload uses streaming requests
To decide whether to enable it, measure the unsafe-request rate, input-rail latency, generation latency, and expected token overhead for your workload. How Speculative Generation Works Without speculative generation, the IORails engine runs the input rails first and only starts the main LLM call after the input rails determine that the input is safe: The engine runs input rails on the user message. If the input is unsafe, it returns the refusal message and stops. If the input is safe, the engine sends the user message to the main LLM and generates a response. The engine runs output rails on the LLM response. If the output is unsafe, it returns the refusal message and stops. The engine returns the response. With speculative generation, the IORails engine starts the input rails and the main LLM call in parallel and waits for whichever finishes first: The engine starts the input rails and the main LLM call in parallel. The engine waits for whichever finishes first, then resolves the race: If the input rails finish first and the input is unsafe, the engine cancels the LLM call and returns the refusal message. If the input rails finish first and the input is safe, the engine waits for the LLM call to finish. If the LLM call finishes first, the engine waits for the input-rail verdict; it discards the response and returns the refusal message if the input is unsafe. The engine runs output rails on the LLM response. The engine returns the response, or the refusal message if output rails blocked it. The IORails engine handles the following outcomes: Outcome Behavior Input rails finish first, input is unsafe The engine cancels the main LLM call. The user receives the refusal message. Input rails finish first, input is safe The engine waits for the main LLM call to finish, then runs output rails. Main LLM finishes first The engine waits for the input-rail verdict. If unsafe, the engine discards the generated response and the user receives the refusal message. If safe, output rails run and return the response. Output rails always run after the main LLM completes
Speculative generation does not change how output rails run. Configuration Example To enable speculative generation, set speculative_generation: True under rails.input in the config.yml file
Speculative generation requires the IORails engine; refer to IORails Engine for how to enable it. models
